title: The Session of Christ
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Meaning of Session
subpoints: Etymology of 'session' as seating to rule
Christ's current ministry as enthroned ruler
Distinction from past works of death and resurrection

outline.title: The Position of Authority
subpoints: The right hand as a place of execution and authority
Heaven as a created realm where Christ is bodily present

outline.title: The Subjection of Powers
subpoints: Angels, authorities, and powers subjected to Christ
The cross as the site of victory over spiritual enemies
Resurrection as the validation of the cross's efficacy

outline.title: The Scope of Christ's Dominion
subpoints: Total authority over the spiritual and physical world
No rogue molecules or beings outside His control
Old Testament foundations in Psalm 2 and Psalm 110

summary:
This sermon explores the theological significance of the ascension and session of Jesus Christ, focusing on 1 Peter 3:22. The speaker clarifies that the 'session' of Christ refers to His current ministry as the enthroned ruler of the universe, seated at the right hand of the Father. This position is not merely one of honor but of active authority and execution, analogous to historical figures like Joseph and Mordecai who held executive power on behalf of kings.

The message emphasizes that the subjection of angels, authorities, and powers to Christ was accomplished through His death on the cross, validated by His resurrection. While the cross appeared as defeat, it was the moment spiritual enemies were triumphed over, a truth confirmed by Christ's subsequent ascension to the highest place in the heavenly realms. This establishes that there is no spiritual or physical entity outside of Christ's sovereign control.

Drawing on Old Testament psalms, particularly Psalm 2 and Psalm 110, the sermon grounds the New Testament teaching of Christ's session in the prophetic expectation of God's anointed king. The ultimate purpose of this sovereign rule is for the benefit of the church, which is united to Christ and thus shares in His resources and authority. Believers are encouraged to find comfort and strength in the knowledge that their Head is the Sovereign Lord over all creation.
